REASONING:
Step 1 – Frame the project  
- **Objective:** Enhance agricultural productivity of small‑ and medium‑scale farmers and improve value‑addition along priority value chains.  
- **Scope & Components:** Five core components (1 Production & productivity, 2 Primary processing & women‑youth empowerment, 3 Infrastructure support, 4 Technical assistance/knowledge/communication, 5 Project management).  
- **Delivery model:** Federal Ministry of Agriculture & Rural Development (FMARD) executes through a National Coordination Office (NCO) and State Coordination Offices (SCOs) in six initial states (Kano, Kaduna, Cross River, Enugu, Lagos, Kogi) with possible expansion to three more.  
- **Timeline:** 23 Mar 2017 – 31 Mar 2023 (6 years).  
- **Budget:** US $200 million (100 % IDA credit).  
- **Key stakeholders:** Federal government, FMARD, NCO, SCOs, State Steering Committees (SSC), State Technical Committees (STC), beneficiaries (farmers, cooperatives, women, youth), private sector, development partners (AfDB, USAID, DFID, etc.).  
- **External dependencies:** Execution of subsidiary agreements, establishment of SCOs, state performance‑based fund releases, procurement capacity, security situation in North East/Niger Delta, environmental safeguards.

Step 2 – Category sweep (risk identified with supporting text ≤ 25 words)  

| # | Category | Description (evidence) |
|---|----------|--------------------------|
| 1 | technical | “low adoption of improved technologies by producers” (Sec 20). |
| 2 | organizational | “procurement capacity is still considered low and most of the states do not have procurement tools” (Sec 89‑90). |
| 3 | financial | “key issues … unretired advances and inadequate documentation of the eligible expenditures incurred” (Sec 88‑89). |
| 4 | financial | “overall FM risk for the project is assessed as Substantial at the preparation phase” (Sec 16). |
| 5 | organizational | “selection and replacement of CADP staff will be completed … following the agreed selection procedures” (Sec 41). |
| 6 | political_regulatory | “No withdrawal shall be made … unless the concerned Participating State has duly established its SCO” (Conditions). |
| 7 | environmental | “possible adverse impacts … use of agricultural chemical inputs … contamination of soils and surface water” (Sec 99‑100). |
| 8 | environmental | “implementation … might pass through important areas and natural habitats … project will strive to stay away” (Natural habitats). |
| 9 | stakeholder | “communities … may submit complaints to existing project‑level grievance redress mechanisms” (Sec 102). |
|10 | political_regulatory | “No withdrawal shall be made … unless the Subsidiary Agreement has been duly authorized or ratified” (Conditions). |
|11 | external | “improving security in the North East and Niger Delta” (Sec 5). |
|12 | financial | “flexible resource allocation … based on performance … states that perform well will be eligible for additional resource allocation” (Sec 40). |
|13 | organizational | “NCO will coordinate … and will be staffed with competitively selected staff that could benefit from TA as required” (Sec 44). |
|14 | organizational | “procurement thresholds … prior review required for contracts above US$750,000” (Sec 16). |
|15 | environmental | “ESMF will ensure that activities … will have no negative environmental impact” (Sec 98). |

Step 3 – Evidence filter  
All listed risks are directly supported by quoted statements; none are removed.

Step 4 – Assess & mitigate  

| ID | Likelihood (1‑5) | Impact (1‑5) | Justification | Mitigation |
|----|-------------------|-------------|---------------|------------|
| R01 | 3 | 4 | Adoption historically low; project provides grants & TA. | Deploy intensive extension (farmer field schools, demo plots), monitor uptake, tie grants to technology use. |
| R02 | 3 | 3 | Many states lack procurement tools; could delay contracts. | Conduct procurement‑capacity workshops, embed third‑party procurement consultants, use standard bidding documents. |
| R03 | 3 | 3 | Unretired advances reported; risk of mis‑use. | Enforce enhanced accountability framework, require pre‑approval, quarterly audits, training on documentation. |
| R04 | 4 | 4 | FM risk rated Substantial; multiple layers increase error chance. | Strengthen PFMUs/FPFMD with computerized accounting, independent internal audit, regular reporting to IDA. |
| R05 | 3 | 3 | Staff replacement needed within first 18 months; possible lag. | Start recruitment early, set firm hiring timelines, monitor progress, use interim staff if needed. |
| R06 | 2 | 4 | Disbursement blocked until SCO legally established. | Prioritize legal ratification of SCOs, assign a monitoring team to track establishment milestones, provide technical assistance. |
| R07 | 3 | 4 | Chemical use can pollute soil/water. | Implement Integrated Pest Management Plan, train on safe pesticide handling, establish buffer zones, conduct runoff monitoring. |
| R08 | 2 | 4 | Infrastructure may intersect sensitive habitats. | Perform environmental screening, avoid identified habitats, apply chance‑find procedures, strict site monitoring. |
| R09 | 3 | 3 | GRM may be overwhelmed, leading to unrest. | Strengthen GRM (hotline, online portal), publicize procedures, ensure 30‑day response, independent oversight committee. |
| R10 | 2 | 5 | Lack of ratified subsidiary agreement stops fund flow. | Obtain legal opinion early, track ratification status, involve senior officials to expedite signing. |
| R11 | 3 | 4 | Security incidents can halt field activities. | Conduct security risk assessments, coordinate with security agencies, adjust field schedules, provide security training for staff. |
| R12 | 3 | 4 | Performance‑based funding may cause cost overruns if estimates are low. | Build realistic budgets with contingencies, quarterly financial reviews, adjust allocations based on verified expenditures. |
| R13 | 3 | 4 | NCO coordinating six states may be overstretched. | Provide TA, hire additional coordination staff, use third‑party support, institute regular performance reviews. |
| R14 | 3 | 3 | Prior‑review thresholds can delay procurement. | Prepare procurement packages well ahead of deadlines, maintain a procurement calendar, engage Bank early for review. |
| R15 | 2 | 5 | Non‑compliance with safeguards can halt the project. | Appoint full‑time environmental specialist, conduct ESIA for all sub‑projects, monitor ESMF compliance, enforce corrective actions. |

Step 5 – Consolidate  
All 15 risks are distinct and supported by the appraisal document; they are retained.
